Expected: No raw weight/alpha/corner literal and no undeclared rx value survives.

Method: Over the shipped dashboard plus seven fixture renders, assert each declared scale step is defined exactly once and that every font-size in a PAINT surface resolves to a declared step - never a raw literal, never a token from another scale. Paint surfaces only, because the rendered document also QUOTES CSS in prose and a whole-document scan judges documentation as code. Also caps the declared set, so a scale cannot grow a step per call site.
Expected: Zero raw font-size literals; every size names a declared step.

Method: Over the shipped dashboard plus seven fixture renders: derive every querySelectorAll selector from the document's own scripts and assert each is classified control-or-not; for every control selector, match its elements in the script-stripped markup (quote-aware tag scan; the tiny selector grammar is matched exactly and anything richer fails loudly) and assert each match is focusable (tabindex=0, a button, or a link with href); assert every classified selector is seen somewhere and every control selector matches at least one element (non-vacuous both ways). Separately assert the only emitted tabindex values are 0 and -1, with -1 confined to roving tablist buttons.
Expected: Every wired control is keyboard-focusable; no unclassified, stale, or non-literal selector; no positive tabindex; every control wiring loop that attaches click/dblclick attaches focus or keydown beside it. Verified to fail against a control losing its tabindex, a newly wired selector (single- AND double-quoted), a positive tabindex, and a wiring loop stripped of its focus path.

Method: Over the shipped dashboard plus seven fixture renders: resolve the document's token definitions, collect every legend swatch carrying a non-empty word label (var() resolved), collect every vocabulary member painted in a PAINT surface of the script-stripped markup (style blocks, style attributes, fill/stroke attributes), and assert each painted member's hex appears as a worded swatch in the SAME document; assert every vocabulary is exercised somewhere in the sweep. Plus the tier-legend bijection: the icicle legend's swatch list equals TIER_FILL in declaration order.
Expected: Every painted vocabulary member is explained in words in its own document; the tier legend is a TIER_FILL bijection (dict-derived, so a dropped member fails); the emitted JS tierColor/statusColor maps byte-match the Python palettes in every render; the CSS status tokens match STATUS_FILL and stay theme-invariant. Verified to fail against the stale hardcoded TC swatch, a legend entry going missing (the legend-less flat seam graph was caught live on this test's first run), the stale JS map (caught live on the committed artifact before its fix), a drifted --done token, and an emitter dropping a tier member.

Method: Reflect every UPPERCASE module-level constant RECURSIVELY (nested dicts/tuples/sets and bare strings) for any 3/4/6/8-digit hex member and assert the hex-bearing set is exactly the five declared vocabularies, every member canonical 6-digit lowercase, and every member clearing 4.5:1 against its label ink (white, or the declared queued dark-ink exception) and 3:1 for its computed _ring_ink. Separately derive every fill:var() token from the emitted CSS and assert each carries a declared role, with white-text-fill roles clearing 4.5:1 under white and container-fill roles keeping --text readable, in BOTH themes. The six sibling A4 tests keep owning their specific arithmetic and are cited as evidence beside the closure.
Parameters: tests/test_gen_trajectory.py (constant math + one with_gate render for the CSS token sweep)
Expected: Vocabulary set closed at five; every member clears both floors; every CSS fill token classified and floor-checked. Verified to fail against a rogue sixth vocabulary (flat AND nested shapes), an under-floor member (2.54:1), and an unclassified fill token.

Method: Generate the dashboard from a zero-active/all-queued fixture (the exact 119-CRITIQUE failure condition) plus a committed module map, then resolve each of the three core reading tasks' entry points from the emitted document and assert each is LABELLED and reachable in <= 1 tab switch: the landing Definition-completeness/Execution cards (task 1, 0 switches), the landing Next-work card (task 2, 0 switches), and the How-SW nav tab (task 3, 1 switch). Assert the next-work surface renders NAMED content (not an empty region) on the zero-active artifact; its non-emptiness across the waiting-with-predecessor and drained fixtures is owned by the cited next-work tests.
Parameters: tests/test_gen_trajectory.py (T1_ALL_QUEUED fixture + ARCH_MD module map; NW_HEADER SafetyClass signal)
Expected: Each task's entry point is present, labelled, and <= 1 switch from the landing view; the next-work surface is non-empty under a zero-active registry. Verified to fail against the next-work surface dropped and against its label emitted empty (guard-bite; source restored byte-identical).

Method: Generate the dashboard and derive EVERY emitted <svg> from the document (not a hand list, so a fourth emitter cannot skip the rule); assert each carries the responsive style and none keeps a bare fixed width; assert the emitted min/max ratio equals the declared SHRINK_FLOOR constant.
Expected: Every emitted svg scales to fit its container; zero svgs keep the pre-fix fixed-width shape; the shrink floor is pinned to the one declared constant rather than re-hardcoded in the test.

Method: Sweep EVERY emitter document (the shipped artifact plus a fixture per emitter, the A2-review rule that a walk judges only what its fixture renders) and, per document: derive the theme-varying/-invariant token families from the emitted CSS; assert exactly one prefers-color-scheme block and one color-scheme declaration, both at :root; assert body's own background and ink are theme-varying; assert no CSS rule pairs a background and an ink from two families; assert no emitted SVG node pairs an inline rect fill with an inline text fill from two families. Then, accumulated ACROSS the sweep (because one document cannot distinguish -paints on the page background- from -this emitter does not render those nodes-), assert every CSS-declared SVG text fill matches the family its host nodes actually paint, or is theme-varying when it has no host anywhere.
Expected: One theme mechanism at :root; zero mixed-family pairs across 900+ classified node pairs and 12 CSS text fills; both families actually occur among the swept rect fills, so the sweep is not vacuous. Guard proven to bite on four independent mutations, each caught by its own assertion: dropping --text from the dark block (half-flip), a phase block's ink switched to var(--text) over its fixed fill, #ice .cell text switched to var(--text) over its invariant host, and a second prefers-color-scheme block scoped to .detail. Source restored byte-identical after each.

Method: Drive gen_open_items over temp repos: assert a pending registry row renders as a brief and a RULED row does not; that Draft AND Modified spine rows both surface (ratification owed vs re-attest owed) while a Verified row does not; that a section with no changed cells says CHECK THE BASELINE and never nothing-changed; that --check bites on drift, MASKS the machine-local region (and still bites outside it), and re-reads the baseline stamp the file declares; that the whole thing is vacuous with neither registry nor view; that registry prose is HTML-escaped; that the word diff marks only what moved and the percentage counts words not whitespace; and that the theme tokens equal the dashboard's emitted values (a drift guard, not an extraction).
Parameters: tests/test_gen_open_items.py (temp repos; one git-backed fixture for the baseline paths)
Expected: Every assertion holds, each with its negative half. Three defects were caught by these guards during the build and fixed rather than accommodated: a missing UTF-8 console guard, a changed-percent diluted by whitespace tokens, and bootstrap leaving __pycache__ in a fresh scaffold once a generator imported its siblings.

Method: Generate the dashboard over a tiered fixture carrying one sentence-length stakeholder need (the shape that overflowed), then sweep EVERY drill block in the emitted document - not a per-view list, because the defect lives in the one shared label emitter that feeds four views. For each block, take its rect and each label line's own x/dy from the markup, measure the line's ink with the emitter's declared per-character widths and the font sizes the emitted CSS declares (unescaping entities first, so an apostrophe is one glyph and not six), and assert the ink box lies inside the rect on both axes. Assert the sentence-length need is actually among the swept labels, so the sweep cannot pass vacuously; separately assert the fit path itself (a second line broken on a word, then an ellipsis, with the full string still reachable) and that a sub-label which already fits keeps the untouched two-line grid. Second half: render the next-work card from a fixture carrying the 109-character clause the critic read and assert it appears WHOLE with no ellipsis in the list, the fixture asserted longer than the retired 60-character budget so the check cannot pass vacuously; then, from a fixture past the declared bound, assert a native details/summary with a visible cue, that the emitted head and remainder rejoin to exactly the clause and the cut fell on a word, and that the reveal is neither script-dependent nor hidden by the emitter's own CSS.
Parameters: tests/test_gen_trajectory.py (_spine_with_a_long_need: 8 SNs, SN-001 carrying the real 138-character need); NW_HEADER fixtures for the next-work card (the 109-character clause the critic read, and one past the bound)
Expected: Zero label lines outside their own block across every drill block of the emitted document; the sentence-length need present among them. Guard proven to bite on the original defect: reverted to the pre-fix emitter it fails naming SN-001's ink at x=-241..449 in a block spanning x=18..190, and the fit-path and helper guards fail with it, while the two-line-grid guard correctly passes both before and after (it guards over-application, not the defect). Source restored byte-identical. Second half: the 109-character clause renders whole; past the bound the disclosure is present, operable and lossless. Both proven to bite on the pre-fix emitter, which renders the critic's exact string 'tiering expo…' and has no _NEXT_WORK_TITLE bound at all. Source restored byte-identical.

Method: Sweep the union of emitter documents (the shipped PROJECT_STATE.html plus a fixture per emitter - the A2-review rule that a walk judges only what its fixture renders) and, per emitted <svg>: parse every node's id and rect and every wire's path data, sample each path into the polyline the router's own hit-test uses (so the test and the emitter describe one curve), drop the rects whose own port circle holds an endpoint, and assert the polyline crosses none of the rest. Assert the sweep found wires at all AND that at least one of them is a DETOUR, so a broken router cannot pass a sweep in which nothing needed re-routing.
Expected: Zero wires through a non-endpoint node box; the sweep non-vacuous (wires present, at least one detoured). Guard proven to bite: with the router's blocked-wire branch disabled so every wire keeps its direct cubic, it fails naming a knowledge-graph wire cutting the 'Low-Level Requirement' node at (330,18,96,46). Source restored byte-identical.
